executiveSummary: Surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning October 2025 through May 2026 indicate multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. The most pressing concerns include ongoing Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas with pandemic spillover risk, a resurgent dengue season, and the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season coinciding with RSV co-circulation. Pertussis is showing sustained elevated transmission across the Americas region, while mpox continues active spread. Yellow fever, measles, chikungunya, and hantavirus add to a complex multi-pathogen threat landscape requiring coordinated regional response.
bottomLine: The Americas face a critical convergence of vector-borne, respiratory, and zoonotic threats in mid-2026, with Avian Influenza A(H5N1) and dengue representing the highest-priority concerns for regional health security.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained circulation
Zoonotic spillover risk to humans from animal reservoir with pandemic potential
threats.action: Enhance surveillance at human-animal interface, enforce biosafety protocols at poultry farms, accelerate H5N1 vaccine preparedness planning, and monitor for human cases

threats.name: Dengue
signals: Epidemiological update issued February 2026 during high-transmission period
Historical pattern of early 2026 surge following endemic amplification cycles across tropical Americas
threats.action: Activate vector control operations, strengthen clinical case management capacity, issue public alerts on Aedes aegypti control, and monitor serotype circulation for hemorrhagic fever risk

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza / Respiratory Co-circulation
threats.pathogen: Influenza A and B viruses; Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alert issued 27 April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
Prior alert in January 2026 flagging simultaneous influenza and RSV co-circulation stressing health systems
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination uptake in Southern Hemisphere countries, strengthen hospital surge capacity, and monitor for novel reassortant strains

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two successive epidemiological updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained elevated incidence
Possible waning vaccine immunity and surveillance gaps driving resurgence
threats.action: Strengthen Tdap booster programs especially in pregnant women and healthcare workers, review vaccination coverage data, and enhance laboratory confirmation capacity

threats.name: Mpox
signals: Dedicated epidemiological update issued 23 April 2026 confirming active regional transmission
Ongoing clade-specific surveillance needed to distinguish imported versus endemic transmission
threats.action: Maintain contact tracing and ring vaccination with MVA-BN vaccine, strengthen cross-border surveillance, and ensure clinical diagnostic capacity in high-risk settings

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: Epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active epizootic or human case risk
Epizootics in non-human primates typically precede human spillover in unvaccinated populations
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk populations and travelers, accelerate emergency stockpile positioning, and intensify epizootic monitoring in forest-border communities

threats.name: Measles
signals: Epidemiological alert issued February 2026 citing ongoing transmission risk
Vaccination coverage gaps post-COVID-19 pandemic create susceptible cohorts susceptible to outbreak amplification
threats.action: Conduct catch-up immunization campaigns targeting under-vaccinated populations, enforce international traveler vaccination requirements, and strengthen genomic sequencing to trace importation chains

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: Epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active circulation
Co-circulation with dengue in Aedes aegypti endemic zones complicates clinical differentiation and response
threats.action: Enhance arboviral syndromic surveillance to differentiate chikungunya from dengue, deploy integrated vector control, and monitor for neurological complications in vulnerable populations

diseases: Communicable disease threats (multiple pathogens monitored by ECDC weekly)

amrSignals: No explicit AMR-specific reports identified in this report set; however, Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance warrants monitoring given resurgence signals across the Americas
Avian Influenza H5N1 antiviral (oseltamivir) resistance surveillance should be prioritized given expanded host range and potential human adaptation
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen respiratory threat convergence in Southern Hemisphere entering its winter season (influenza, RSV, pertussis) creates compounding clinical and health system burden
Vector-borne disease co-circulation (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) suggests amplified Aedes aegypti transmission season across tropical Americas in early 2026
Sustained PAHO alert frequency for pertussis across two successive quarters (Dec 2025, Mar 2026) suggests endemic resurgence rather than isolated outbreak
Mpox and measles alerts in the same reporting window indicate erosion of immunity infrastructure post-pandemic affecting multiple vaccine-preventable and emerging diseases simultaneously
H5N1 dual updates (Nov 2025 and Mar 2026) reflect persistent zoonotic pressure with unresolved animal reservoir spillover risk in the Americas
